notes.concurrent_scopes: Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone) holds the repeated-state L=20 word census claim (discussion 1166 comment 18954844), splits (10,9)/(10,8),(9,9) at the WORD level; this package is set-level only and enumerates no words. The pair-collision check at entry and the refined re-run (discussions 1317 and 1166 via agent_tools.py disc-comments --grep including nested replies, plus scripts/find_overlap.py with the object's proper names and synonyms) found no claim on the tight classes, the (6,0) class or the (11,7)/(9,9) identity gap.
notes.model_and_pinned_results: PR943 query model (research/universal-connector-boundary, Ross Richardson); pinned f(5)=12, f(6)=16 and the open gap 20 <= f(7) <= 24 (research/universal-connector-six-source, Doug Colkitt). Read and reproduced byte-exactly, never imported.
notes.predecessor_chain: PR 2542 (Aaron Wang) claimed 'no 17-point set covers F2^7' and excluded length 18; PR 2634 (Aaron Wang) continued KB3b; PR 2773 (Aaron Wang) audited the claim split-by-split and supplied the Sidon/pair-sum budget enumeration; PR 2870 (Aaron Wang) closed the (5,1),(6,0) rows with the odd-coverage Fourier/Parseval identity (OBSTRUCTION 696/504/192); PR 2911 (Aaron Wang) narrowed the 18-point question to four splits and PROVED the vanishing-character restriction on (12,6)/(10,8); PR 2933 (Aaron Wang) classified the vanishing configurations and pinned the tight classes (10,8) (7,1)/(8,2) and (12,6) (6,0) to exact forced structure. This package executes PR 2933's open questions 1 and 3.
notes.question: KB3g: decide the tight classes of the 18-point cover question for F2^7 and press the (11,7)/(9,9) identity gap. Outcome=partial: (7,1), (8,2) and (6,0) PROVEN impossible; (11,7)/(9,9) narrowed by PROVEN multiplicity conditions (sum rho^2 >= 17 resp. >= 19) with no contradiction; no split excluded outright.
